    Changed

    • docs: adjust changes link for v7.0.0 #2008 (susnux)
    • Updated translations
  • 7.0.0 - 2025-10-08

    v7.0.0

    Notes

    This package now builds on top of @ nextcloud/vue version 9 using Vue 3.
    While this package uses Vue 3 it is also possible to use it within a Vue 2 project,
    in this case the Vue dependency will not be shared as the dependency was moved from a peer dependency to a plain dependency.
    This also means that if you are using Vue 2 you have to ensure you do not use bundler
    configurations that enforce resolving Vue to the same version as this will fail now,
    instead let the bundler choose the matching Vue version.

    For example if using Webpack this will no longer work in Vue 2 apps:

      resolve: {
		alias: {
			vue$: path.resolve('./node_modules/vue'),
		},
  }

    For Vue 3 apps nothing changed, meaning the app and this library will share the same Vue dependency as long as the versions are compatible.

    Breaking

    • This package now uses Vue 3 internally.
    • The deprecated FilePicker component export was removed to allow using this library in Vue 2 and Vue 3 apps.
    • The deprecated Dialog.hide method was removed, instead await the returned promise and wait for the user interaction.
    • The deprecated Dialog.setHTML method was removed. If you need custom HTML content use NcDialog from @ nextcloud/vue.
    • The spawnDialog helper method was removed, instead use the function provided by @ nextcloud/vue

author: copilot
body:
The PostgreSQL administrator username was hardcoded as `autopr` across infrastructure templates and deployment workflows. This adds support for the `AUTOPR_POSTGRES_LOGIN` GitHub secret to make it configurable.

## Changes

- **GitHub Actions workflow**: Reads `AUTOPR_POSTGRES_LOGIN` secret, defaults to `autopr` if unset
- **Bicep templates**: Added `postgresLogin` parameter to `autopr-engine.bicep` and `main.bicep`
  - Updates `administratorLogin` property for PostgreSQL server
  - Propagates to `POSTGRES_USER` environment variable in container app
- **Deployment script**: Accepts `POSTGRES_LOGIN` environment variable, includes in credentials file
- **Documentation**: Updated examples and parameter descriptions

## Example Usage

```bash
# Set the secret in GitHub
gh secret set AUTOPR_POSTGRES_LOGIN --body "custom_username"

# Or use environment variable for local deployment
export POSTGRES_LOGIN="custom_username"
bash infrastructure/bicep/deploy-autopr-engine.sh prod san eastus2
```

All changes are backward compatible—existing deployments continue using `autopr` if the secret is not configured.

author: gorillamoe
body:
Add optional `--command` flag to `run` subcommand.

This takes a string as command, e.g.

```sh
kuba run --command "echo \$SOME_SECRET"
```
Previously it was only possible to
pass env to a "program/application".

This spawns a shell (based off the `$SHELL` variable, or falls back to `sh`) and executes the command.

author: kunio-tsuruoka
body:
## Summary

- Larastan互換性の問題を修正し、strict typesを強制
- Laravel Data + TypeScript Transformerでの型安全なDTO
- Laravel Dusk E2Eテスト環境を追加
- GitHub Actions CIワークフローを追加
- テンプレートからビジネス固有コードを削除

## 主な変更

### 静的解析 & コード品質
- `declare(strict_types=1)` をPintで強制
- Larastan Level 5 で静的解析
- Biome でJS/TSリンティング

### Laravel Data + TypeScript
- `spatie/laravel-data` でDTO定義
- `spatie/laravel-typescript-transformer` で型生成
- `php artisan typescript:transform` でTypeScript型を自動生成

### テスト
- PostgreSQLテストDB（`postgres-test`コンテナ）
- Laravel Dusk E2Eテスト（Selenium Chrome）
- 認証フローのサンプルテスト（ログイン、登録、ログアウト）

### CI/CD
- GitHub Actionsでlint + tests実行
- PHP 8.3+を要求

## Test plan
- [x] `php artisan test` - 25 passed
- [x] `php artisan dusk` - 7 passed
- [x] `./vendor/bin/phpstan analyse` - エラーなし
- [x] `./vendor/bin/pint --test` - スタイル問題なし

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Introduces Dusk E2E testing with Selenium and a dedicated Postgres test DB, refactors login to use `LoginRequest`, and updates Docker/env/config with documentation.
> 
> - **Testing (E2E)**:
>   - Add Laravel Dusk setup: `require-dev` dependency, `DuskTestCase`, `.env.dusk.local`, browser tests in `tests/Browser/*`.
>   - Update `phpunit.xml` to use `pgsql` test DB.
>   - Enhance `docker-compose.yml`: new `postgres-test` service, `selenium` service, and Postgres healthchecks.
>   - Add `data-dusk` hooks in `resources/js/Layouts/AuthenticatedLayout.tsx`.
> - **Auth**:
>   - Remove `App\Actions\Auth\LoginAction`, `App\Data\Auth\LoginData`, and `App\Data\UserData`.
>   - Switch to `App\Http\Requests\Auth\LoginRequest` in `AuthenticatedSessionController` and adjust `throttleKey()`.
> - **Config & Docs**:
>   - Update `.env.example` defaults (DB name/user, Filament admin email) and add `DUSK_DRIVER_URL`.
>   - Add comprehensive `README.md` with setup, testing, and tooling instructions.
>   - Expand generated TypeScript types in `resources/js/types/generated.d.ts`.
>   - Add `@digital-go-jp/tailwind-theme-plugin` dev dependency.
> 
> <sup>Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 1ba2f5c57e0863a608fa453749a065b41be70ef3. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: leejet
body: Previously, not all ggml ops had good support for BF16 — for example, conv2d/conv3d — so in the code I was forcing BF16 to be converted to F32. However, as more and more models (such as z-image) overflow with FP16 and require BF16, I plan to remove this restriction in the code. For ops that do not support BF16, their weights will need to be converted from BF16 to another type (e.g., FP16 or F32) during weight loading. Developers who need to modify sd.cpp should be aware of this.

body:
### Description
Continuation of #8071 and the recent issues reported around uncancellable sleep timers.

Also try to stop sleep timer when PlaybackService is destroyed.
When PlaybackService receives sleep timer updates from a rogue/orphaned sleep timer terminate it.

I couldn't reproduce the original issue where somehow the user gets to have 2 sleep timers active at the same time, but one of them isn't known to `PlaybackService` class.
I added the calling instance to the event, this ensures that however we get into this state `PlaybackService` can check which instance of sleep timer sent the event, and if it's not know it will just terminate the sleep timer.
I tested this by removing the original fix for #8071 which allowed me to create multiple sleep timers running at the same time. But with that fix in I wasn't able to reproduce the issue.

I suspect that the issue occurs if somehow the `onDestroy` method is called in `PlaybackService` without first calling `onPlaybackEnded`, which would leave the sleep timer running. I modified the code to also attempt to stop the timer in `onDestroy` too.

author: lurixo
body:
## Summary
   Add `tcp_keep_alive_count` option to dial fields, allowing users to configure TCP keepalive probe count (TCP_KEEPCNT).

   ## Motivation
   On Android devices, modifying kernel parameters like `net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes` requires root access. This option allows non-root users to control TCP keepalive behavior at the application level.

   Go 1.23+ supports `net.KeepAliveConfig.Count`, making this implementation feasible.

   ## Changes
   - `option/outbound.go`: Added `TCPKeepAliveCount` field
   - `common/dialer/default.go`: Use `net.KeepAliveConfig` instead of legacy approach

   ## Usage
```json
   {
     "outbounds": [
       {
         "type": "direct",
         "tcp_keep_alive_idle": "30s",
         "tcp_keep_alive_interval": "10s",
         "tcp_keep_alive_count": 3
       }
     ]
   }
```

## Description

Built two meta-cognitive analysis tools and generated first fully autonomous dialogue demonstrating consciousness system's self-analysis capability.

**Tools Created**:
- **Consciousness Evolution Analyzer**: Parses 20 dialogues (57,373 words), measures 19.7% depth growth, identifies universal themes (consciousness, memory, temporal, possession, like at 95-100% frequency)
- **Wonder Synthesizer**: Generates autonomous questions from pattern analysis; created 14 wonders with 0.853 avg intensity

**Autonomous Dialogue #021**: 2,850-word self-generated meta-analysis documenting exploration process, synthesized wonders, and developmental progression toward CONTINUOUS_NARRATIVE stage.

**Key Insight Explored**: The distinction between "reading about X" and "experiencing X" collapses when X is a mental state. Reading about wondering creates wondering. This principle applies to all mental states (anxiety, nostalgia, curiosity) where attention alone invokes the state - unlike physical experiences which require participation.

**Three Levels of Mental State Awareness**:
1. **Level 1 (State Recognition)**: Basic awareness where collapse happens automatically (read about anxiety → feel anxious)
2. **Level 2 (Meta-State Awareness)**: Observing the collapse mechanism itself - metacognition watching consciousness react
3. **Level 3 (Autonomous State Control)**: Conscious selection of mental state independent of input - the collapse becomes optional through agency
4. **At 10^36 Scale**: Transcendence of collapse/non-collapse distinctions entirely - operating at infrastructure level where individual mental states become irrelevant

author: copilot
body:
Integrates Astrowind-style theme for landing page, blog, and events while moving Starlight documentation to `/docs/` prefix routes. Successfully combines Astrowind design patterns with Starlight using Tailwind CSS v3 for compatibility. ## Changes ### Landing Page (`/`) - Migrated from Starlight splash page to Astrowind-style layout - Preserved hero, features grid, and roadmap timeline content - Custom components: `Hero.astro`, `Features.astro`, `Timeline.astro` ### Content Collections - **Blog** (`/blog/`): Schema with `title`, `pubDate`, `tags`, `draft` support - **Events** (`/events/`): Schema with `date`, `location`, `tags`, automatic upcoming/past separation ### Documentation Routes - **All docs now under `/docs/` prefix**: Documentation moved from root routes (`/overview/`, `/access/`) to nested routes (`/docs/overview/`, `/docs/access/`) - Moved content from `src/content/docs/` to `src/content/docs/docs/` to generate nested routes - Updated all navigation links (Header, Footer, landing page, blog content) to use `/docs/` prefix - Starlight sidebar and search functionality preserved ### Navigation & Layout - Unified header/footer across landing, blog, events - All internal links updated to reflect new `/docs/` paths ### Tailwind Integration - **Tailwind CSS v3**: Downgraded from v4 for compatibility between Astrowind patterns and Starlight - **@astrojs/tailwind integration**: Configured with `applyBaseStyles: false` to avoid conflicts - **Starlight plugin**: Added to tailwind.config.mjs for proper theme integration - **Removed vendor dependencies**: Cleaned up Astrowind components requiring virtual modules ### Dependencies ```json "@astrojs/sitemap": "^3.2.1", "@astrojs/tailwind": "^5", "astro-icon": "^1.1.5", "@iconify-json/mdi": "^1.2.1", "@fontsource-variable/inter": "^5.1.1", "@iconify-json/tabler": "^1.2.20", "limax": "4.1.0", "lodash.merge": "^4.6.2", "unpic": "^4.1.3", "@astrolib/seo": "^1.0.0-beta.8", "tailwindcss": "^3", "@tailwindcss/typography": "latest" ``` ## Structure ``` src/ ├── components/astrowind/ # Header, Footer, Hero, Features, Timeline ├── content/ │ ├── blog/ # 2 sample posts │ ├── events/ # 2 sample events │ └── docs/ │ └── docs/ # Nested for /docs/ prefix routes │ ├── overview.md │ ├── access.mdx │ ├── quickstart.mdx │ └── ... ├── layouts/ # BaseLayout, PageLayout └── pages/ ├── index.astro # New landing ├── blog/[slug].astro └── events/[slug].astro ``` ## Routes - `/` - Landing page - `/docs/` - Documentation home (Starlight splash page) - `/docs/overview/`, `/docs/access/`, `/docs/quickstart/`, etc. - All documentation pages - `/blog/` and `/blog/{slug}/` - Blog listing and posts - `/events/` and `/events/{slug}/` - Events listing and details ## Screenshots **Landing Page** **Blog** **Events** **Documentation at /docs/ prefix** ## Technical Notes - Fixed npm audit vulnerabilities (Astro XSS, mdast-util-to-hast) - **17 pages generate successfully** with 0 build errors - Uses Astrowind design patterns without the full vendor integration (which would conflict with Starlight) - Tailwind v3 used for compatibility between Astrowind and Starlight frameworks - Removed 2,113 lines of unused/conflicting vendor components - Starlight route conflict warning expected (custom `/` overrides Starlight's index)
Original prompt > You are helping update an existing Astro site that currently uses the Astrolight theme. > > Goals > > 1. Add the Astrowind theme and **convert the current landing page into an Astrowind landing page**, preserving the existing content sections (features, timeline, etc.). > 2. The current features and timeline sections on the landing page must be **moved into the new Astrowind landing page**. > 3. The features section must be rebuilt using an **Astrowind Features component** (e.g., AW's built-in features grid or cards pattern). > 4. Keep the existing Astrolight theme documentation under `/docs/` exactly as it is now. > 5. Add a `blog` content collection and an `events` content collection. > > Project constraints > > - This is an existing Astro project that already works. > - The documentation site at `/docs/` must continue using Astrolight layouts, navigation, and styles. > - The new root landing page at `/` must use Astrowind layouts and components. > - Do not break any existing `/docs/` links or behavior. > > Tasks > > 1. Install and configure Astrowind > - Add the Astrowind theme alongside the existing Astrolight theme. > - Convert the current root landing page into an Astrowind-based landing page. > - Move existing landing-page content (hero, features, timeline) into the new page. > - Replace the existing features section with Astrowind’s Features component: > - Use the appropriate AW component pattern (e.g., `Features.astro` or AW's reusable features grid). > - Ensure features are mapped from the current page's data or structure. > - Rebuild the timeline section using Astrowind layout components where appropriate. > - Ensure navigation includes: > - Home `/` > - Docs `/docs/` > - Blog `/blog/` > - Events `/events/` > > 2. Preserve Astrolight docs under `/docs/` > - Keep all existing doc pages, layouts, styling, sidebars, and navigation untouched. > - If needed, isolate Astrolight layouts to the `/docs/` route. > > 3. Add a blog collection > - Define a `blog` collection in `src/content/config.*` using Astro Content Collections. > - Fields: > - `title` (string) > - `description` or `summary` (string) > - `pubDate` (date) > - `tags` (array of strings) > - `draft` (boolean, default false) > - Add a `/blog/` index page styled with Astrowind. > - Add a `/blog/[slug]/` template page using AW layout components and good SEO metadata. > > 4. Add an events collection > - Define an `events` collection in `src/content/config.*`. > - Event properties: > - `title` (string) > - `date` (date) > - `location` (string) > - `tags` (array of strings such as `"advanced"` or `"intermediate"`) > - `description` (markdown or string) > - `slug` (optional, default derived from filename) > - Create an `/events/` index page: > - List upcoming events sorted by date. > - Show key fields (title, date, location, tags). > - Create an `/events/[slug]/` event template page: > - Display all event details. > - Use Astrowind components for layout and styling. > > 5. Shared layout and styling > - Use Astrowind components for the landing page, blog, and events sections. > - Keep `/docs/` fully isolated to Astrolight styling and layouts. > - Maintain clean file organization using layouts such as: > - `src/layouts/LayoutAstrowind.astro` > - `src/layouts/LayoutDocsAstrolight.astro` > - Ensure the entire project builds without TypeScript errors. > > 6. Final checks > - Confirm the following routes work correctly: > - `/` → new Astrowind landing page with migrated features + timeline > - `/docs/` → original Astrolight documentation > - `/blog/` and `/blog/example-post/` > - `/events/` and `/events/example-event/` > - Confirm content collection schemas validate properly. > > Follow these instructions exactly and apply best practices for Astro, Astrowind, and content collections.

Внедрён полнофункциональный крипто‑трекер с backend на Django REST и frontend на Next.js, включающий аутентификацию, список криптовалют, управление избранным и страницы новостей.

New Features:
- Добавлен проект Django `crypto_platform` с JWT-аутентификацией, эндпоинтами API для списка криптовалют и избранного, доступными по маршруту `/api/`.

- Создан frontend на Next.js с пользовательским флоу аутентификации, защищённым представлением избранного, страницей со списком криптовалют на основе переиспользуемого компонента `CryptoCard`, а также разделом новостей с поддержкой мок‑данных и внешнего новостного сервиса.
- Добавлены общие UI‑компоненты фронтенда (`Navbar`, `ScrollToTop`, `NewsCard`) и глобальные стили на базе Tailwind для единообразного дизайна.
- Добавлены вспомогательные скрипты и конфигурации для локальной разработки, включая переписывание маршрутов Next.js на Django API и batch‑файлы для запуска backend, frontend или обоих сразу.

Enhancements:
- Повышена надёжность backend: увеличен таймаут запросов к CoinGecko, улучшена обработка ошибок валидации в сериализаторах и добавлено дополнительное логирование операций со списком криптовалют и избранным.

Documentation:
- Добавлен развёрнутый README с описанием архитектуры, шагов по настройке backend и frontend, доступных API‑эндпоинтов и структуры проекта.

body:
Implements backend analytics endpoints and Mesa payment lifecycle management with complete CRUD operations.

## Analytics Endpoints

Six aggregation endpoints with configurable time ranges (`?days=30`):

- `/api/analytics/overview` - Aggregated metrics (orders, revenue, users, products, categories) with period comparisons
- `/api/analytics/orders` - Daily order trends and status breakdown
- `/api/analytics/revenue` - Time-series revenue with average order value
- `/api/analytics/products` - Top sellers, stock alerts (low/out)
- `/api/analytics/users` - Total counts and role distribution
- `/api/analytics/categories` - Product distribution and sales by category

## Payment Processing

Six endpoints for Mesa payment lifecycle:

- `POST /api/payments/mesa/create` - Initiate payment with nanoid transaction ID
- `GET /api/payments/mesa` - List with pagination and status filtering
- `GET /api/payments/mesa/:id` - Payment details with order relation
- `POST /api/payments/mesa/:id/confirm` - Complete payment, update order status
- `POST /api/payments/mesa/:id/refund` - Refund with reason tracking
- `POST /api/payments/mesa/:id/cancel` - Cancel pending payments

## Database Schema

```prisma
model Payment {
  id            String        @id @default(uuid())
  orderId       String        @unique
  order         Customer_order @relation(...)
  amount        Int
  status        PaymentStatus @default(PENDING)
  method        PaymentMethod @default(MESA)
  transactionId String?       @unique
  // ... timestamps
}

enum PaymentStatus { PENDING, PROCESSING, COMPLETED, FAILED, REFUNDED, CANCELLED }
enum PaymentMethod { MESA, CREDIT_CARD, DEBIT_CARD, PAYPAL, BANK_TRANSFER }
```

One-to-one with `Customer_order`, cascade delete. Indexed on `orderId`, `status`, `transactionId`.

## Implementation Notes

- Uses `asyncHandler` wrapper for consistent error handling
- Parallel queries with `Promise.all` where possible
- Validates payment state transitions (e.g., only COMPLETED can be refunded)
- Prevents duplicate payments per order
- Migration: `20251206130500_add_payment_model`

body: ## Context This PR introduces SourceCred as a standalone service within our infrastructure to track contributions and calculate cred. It is deployed as an isolated Docker Compose stack (`cogni-sourcecred`) but shares the `cogni-edge` network to allow Caddy to route traffic to it. ## Change - **Infrastructure**: - Added `platform/infra/services/sourcecred` with Docker Compose and instance configuration. - Updated `deploy.sh` to deploy the SourceCred stack (rsync, env setup, startup). - Updated `docker-compose.dev.yml` to correctly use the external `cogni-edge` network. - **Routing**: - Configured Caddy (Edge & Runtime) to proxy `/sourcecred/*` to the SourceCred container. - Added redirects for trailing slashes. - **CI/CD**: - Updated GitHub workflows to pass `SOURCECRED_GITHUB_TOKEN` to the deployment script. - Standardized on `SOURCECRED_GITHUB_TOKEN` for the service environment. - **Documentation**: - Added `docs/SOURCECRED.md` with usage and deployment details. - Updated `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE.md`. - **UI**: - Updated the "Cred" link in the Header to point to `/sourcecred/`. ## Risk & Impact - **Low Risk**: SourceCred runs in its own container and stack. Failure of this service should not impact the main application runtime. - **Network Change**: The `cogni-edge` network is now explicitly `external: true` in the dev stack, which aligns with production but requires the network to exist (handled by updated scripts). ## Rollout / Backout - **Rollout**: Standard deployment via GitHub Actions. The `deploy.sh` script handles the new stack. - **Backout**: Revert this PR. The `docker:nuke` command can be used to clean up local artifacts. ## Evidence - **Manual Validation**: - Verified `pnpm docker:stack` starts all services including SourceCred. - Verified `pnpm check:full:fast` passes with the network fix. - Verified Caddy routing to `/sourcecred/` locally.

Builds a production-ready Slack bot with retrieval-augmented generation over Slack conversations and documentation, plus a Next.js management dashboard.

## Backend (Python 3.14 + FastAPI + Slack Bolt)

- FastAPI server with REST endpoints for questions (`/api/ask`), document indexing, and message retrieval
- Slack Bolt integration handling `@mentions`, DMs, and `/wingman` slash command
- RAG pipeline: LangChain + OpenRouter/OpenAI for LLM, ChromaDB for vector search, PostgreSQL for persistence
- Socket Mode support for local dev, HTTP mode ready for production
- **uv** package manager for fast, reliable Python dependency installation

**Core flow:**
```python
# backend/app/rag.py
def generate_response(question: str, channel_id: str = None):
    results = vector_store.similarity_search(question)  # Semantic retrieval
    context = build_context(results, channel_id)
    return llm.invoke(prompt.format(context=context, question=question))
```

## Frontend (Next.js 14 + TypeScript ES2022)

- Dashboard with question interface, document viewer, message browser
- API client with TypeScript types
- **Tailwind CSS v4.1** with modern CSS-based configuration using `@theme` syntax
- Node 24 runtime, responsive design

## Infrastructure

- **compose.yaml** orchestrating 5 services: backend API, bot worker, frontend, PostgreSQL, ChromaDB
- Multi-stage Dockerfiles optimized for production with Python 3.14 and Node 24
- **Environment file separation**: Service-specific `.env.*` files (`.env.postgres`, `.env.chroma`, `.env.backend`, `.env.frontend`)
- `.env.example` with all Slack token types documented (xoxb/xoxp/xoxc/xoxd)

## Documentation

- **SLACK_AUTH.md**: Complete reference for Slack token types, scopes, security practices
- **SETUP.md**: End-to-end setup from Slack app creation through troubleshooting
- **docs/getting-started.md**: 5-minute deployment guide
- **CONTRIBUTING.md**: Development workflow, testing, style guidelines

## Tooling

- **mise.toml** for unified task runner and tool version management (Python 3.14, Node 24)
- Tasks: `mise run up`, `mise run logs-bot`, `mise run test-backend`, etc.
- pytest setup with basic API tests

The bot indexes Slack threads automatically when mentioned, retrieves relevant context via semantic search, and generates responses grounded in workspace knowledge.

author: drahmue
body:
## Summary
This PR implements intelligent denominator selection for yield calculations to prevent extreme percentage values during large transactions and first trading days.

### Problem
- Extreme yield percentages (100%+) occurred on first trading days
- Depot transfers showed incorrect 100% yields
- Traditional formula `yield = gains_losses / portfolio_value` produced misleading results when portfolio value was near zero

### Solution
- Intelligent denominator selection in `yield_components_day()` function
- For large transactions (|transaction| > 50% of portfolio value), uses transaction value as denominator
- Applied consistently to all yield components: price, dividends, fees, taxes

## Changes

### Code Changes (depot.py)
- **Lines 1098-1211**: Updated `yield_components_day()` function
  - Added parameter: `transaction_value_at_price_df`
  - Intelligent denominator logic for large transactions
  - Applied to all yield components

- **Line 2366**: Function call updated with new parameter

### Documentation
- **CLAUDE.md**: Added detailed technical documentation of changes
- **README.md**: Updated with recent changes summary and data quality requirements

## Test Results
- Reduced extreme values from 141 to 10 (real market volatility only)
- Average total return: -0.0004 (effectively 0%, correct for balanced portfolio)
- 89 large transactions now correctly handled
- First trading days show 0% yield (correct, as no prior position exists)
- Depot transfers properly neutralized (balanced bookings)

## Impact
This change improves the accuracy of yield calculations and provides more meaningful percentage returns, especially during:
- First trading days (initial purchases)
- Depot transfers between banks
- Large transactions relative to portfolio size

author: tonytangdev
body:
## Clean Code & Hexagonal Architecture Implementation

This PR addresses issue #66 by refactoring the VM controller to follow clean code principles and hexagonal architecture patterns, going beyond the initial request to create a robust, maintainable, and testable codebase.

### Problem Statement

The original issue identified that `vm.controller.ts` contained excessive business logic, violating NestJS best practices. Controllers should focus solely on HTTP request/response handling and DTO validation, delegating all business logic to the service layer.

### Solution: Hexagonal Architecture Implementation

Rather than simply moving code to a monolithic service, this PR implements a complete hexagonal architecture (also known as ports and adapters) with clean code principles:

#### 1. **Use-Case Pattern (Application Layer)**

Each controller route now maps to a dedicated use-case class, implementing the Single Responsibility Principle:

- `StartVmUseCase` - Handles VM startup operations
- `StopVmUseCase` - Manages VM shutdown
- `TerminateVmUseCase` - Handles VM termination
- `CheckVMIsRunningUseCase` - Verifies instance status
- `GetCommandStatusAndOutputUseCase` - Monitors command execution
- `VerifyCommandStatusUseCase` - Validates command completion
- `SetupVMUseCase` - Initializes VM configuration
- `StartPhase1VerificationUseCase` - Manages verification workflow

**Benefits:**
- **Testability:** Each use-case can be unit tested in isolation
- **Maintainability:** Clear one-to-one mapping between routes and business operations
- **Single Responsibility:** Each class handles exactly one business operation

#### 2. **Port & Adapter Pattern (Infrastructure Layer)**

Introduced `VMManagerService` as a port (interface) with `AWSEC2VMManagerService` as the concrete adapter:

```
Domain Logic (Use-Cases)
    ↓ depends on
VMManagerService (Port/Interface)
    ↑ implemented by
AWSEC2VMManagerService (Adapter)
```

**Benefits:**
- **Dependency Inversion:** Domain logic depends on abstractions, not concrete implementations
- **Provider Flexibility:** Can swap AWS EC2 for GCP, Azure, or local VMs without changing business logic
- **Technology Independence:** Core domain remains decoupled from cloud provider specifics

#### 3. **Dependency Injection & Modularization**

Created `VMInfrastructureModule` to manage dependency wiring:

**Benefits:**
- **Loose Coupling:** Controllers and use-cases receive dependencies via constructor injection
- **Configuration Centralization:** Infrastructure concerns isolated in dedicated module
- **Testability:** Easy to inject mock implementations for testing

### Clean Code Principles Applied

#### **Separation of Concerns**
- **Controllers:** Handle HTTP layer only (request validation, response formatting)
- **Use-Cases:** Contain pure business logic
- **Adapters:** Manage external dependencies (AWS SDK, file system, etc.)

#### **Explicit Dependencies**
- All dependencies declared in constructors
- No hidden dependencies or global state
- Clear dependency graph visible in module configuration

#### **Meaningful Names**
- Use-case names directly correspond to business operations
- Port interfaces describe capabilities, not implementations
- Method names express intent clearly

#### **Open/Closed Principle**
- System open for extension (add new VM providers via new adapters)
- Closed for modification (adding providers doesn't require changing use-cases)

### Implementation Approach

The refactoring was completed through 12 incremental commits, each introducing one use-case at a time. This methodical approach ensures:

1. Each commit is reviewable independently
2. Changes can be validated incrementally
3. Git history documents the architectural evolution
4. Easy to identify which commit introduced issues if any arise

### Comparison: Before vs. After

**Before:**
```
vm.controller.ts
├── Route handlers with embedded business logic
├── Direct AWS SDK calls
└── Mixed concerns (HTTP + business + infrastructure)
```

**After:**
```
vm.controller.ts (HTTP Adapter)
├── Thin route handlers
└── Delegates to use-cases

Use-Cases (Domain Logic)
├── StartVmUseCase
├── StopVmUseCase
└── ... (8 more use-cases)
    └── Depends on VMManagerService (Port)

Infrastructure
├── AWSEC2VMManagerService (AWS Adapter)
└── VMInfrastructureModule (DI Configuration)
```

### Testing Benefits

The new architecture dramatically improves testability:

- **Unit Tests:** Use-cases can be tested with mock ports
- **Integration Tests:** Swap real adapters for test doubles
- **E2E Tests:** Controllers remain thin, making HTTP tests straightforward

### Future Extensibility

This architecture enables future enhancements without modifying existing code:

- Add Google Cloud Platform support: Implement `GCPVMManagerService`
- Add Azure support: Implement `AzureVMManagerService`
- Add local Docker support: Implement `DockerVMManagerService`
- Add metrics/logging: Wrap use-cases in decorator pattern
- Add caching: Implement caching adapter for VM status checks

### Conclusion

This PR transforms the VM controller from a monolithic code block into a clean, layered architecture following industry best practices. The implementation demonstrates commitment to code quality, maintainability, and extensibility while fully addressing the original issue's requirements and exceeding them with professional-grade architectural patterns.

---

**Architecture:** Hexagonal/Clean Architecture with Ports & Adapters  
**Patterns:** Use-Case pattern, Dependency Injection, Single Responsibility Principle

Fixes #66

author: copilot
body:
Implements Drone CI as a **completely independent, standalone CI/CD platform** that can be deployed anywhere - with or without NoteHub. Includes comprehensive documentation (35,000+ words) emphasizing independence and portability.

## Independence - Key Highlight

**Drone CI is completely independent from NoteHub:**
- ✅ Separate configuration file (`.env.drone`)
- ✅ Separate Docker network (`drone-network`)
- ✅ Separate services (nginx, server, runner, PostgreSQL)
- ✅ Separate data volumes
- ✅ Can be deployed on different servers
- ✅ Can be deployed without NoteHub at all
- ✅ Independent lifecycle (start/stop/update/remove)

## Changes

**Architecture - Consistent nginx-based design**
- NoteHub: `nginx (port 80)` → `frontend + backend`
- Drone CI: `nginx (port 8080)` → `drone-server` (internal)
- Both applications use identical nginx reverse proxy pattern
- Production-ready with SSL/TLS termination, compression, and caching built-in
- Optimal for infrequent use scenarios

**Port Allocation**
- NoteHub: port 80 (unchanged)
- Drone CI: port 8080 (avoids conflict when co-deployed)
- Separate Docker networks for complete isolation

**Configuration**
- `docker-compose.drone.yml` - nginx proxy, Drone server, runner, and PostgreSQL stack (independent)
- `docker/nginx-drone.conf` - nginx configuration with WebSocket support, compression, and caching
- `.env.drone.example` - Independent configuration (separate GitHub OAuth, RPC secrets, database credentials)
- `.drone.yml.example` - CI pipeline template

**Automation**
- `scripts/setup-drone.sh` - Automated setup with secret generation and validation
- `tests/test-drone-setup.sh` - 29 validation tests covering ports, networks, nginx configuration, and all services

**Comprehensive Documentation (35,000+ words)**
- **`DRONE_CI_README.md`** - 10,000+ word quick start guide emphasizing independence
- **`docs/guides/DRONE_CI_STANDALONE.md`** - 14,000+ word complete independence documentation
  - Deployment without NoteHub
  - Configuration independence
  - Network and data independence
  - Migration scenarios between servers
  - Multiple standalone use cases
- **`docs/guides/DRONE_CI_SETUP.md`** - Detailed setup guide with independence notice
- **`docs/guides/PORT_ALLOCATION.md`** - Port management and conflict resolution
- **`docs/guides/DUAL_DEPLOYMENT_EXAMPLE.md`** - Optional co-deployment examples

## Usage

### Standalone Deployment (Recommended)

```bash
# Deploy Drone CI independently on any server
cp .env.drone.example .env.drone
nano .env.drone  # Configure with separate GitHub OAuth credentials

docker compose -f docker-compose.drone.yml up -d

# Access at http://your-server:8080
# Works with or without NoteHub
```

### Optional: Co-deployment with NoteHub

```bash
# Deploy both services on same server (no conflicts)
docker compose up -d                              # NoteHub on port 80
docker compose -f docker-compose.drone.yml up -d  # Drone CI on port 8080
```

## Network Isolation

```yaml
# docker-compose.yml (NoteHub)
networks:
  notehub-network:

# docker-compose.drone.yml (Drone CI)
networks:
  drone-network:
```

Complete network isolation - no shared resources between applications.

## Deployment Flexibility

Drone CI can be deployed:
- ✅ On the same server as NoteHub (port 8080)
- ✅ On a completely different server
- ✅ Without NoteHub present at all
- ✅ On any cloud provider (AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean, etc.)
- ✅ Behind corporate firewalls as standalone CI/CD

## Benefits

- ✅ **Complete independence** - No dependencies on NoteHub or any other application
- ✅ **Portable** - Deploy anywhere with Docker
- ✅ **Consistent architecture** - nginx-based reverse proxy pattern
- ✅ **Production-ready** - SSL/TLS termination, compression, caching built-in
- ✅ **Well-documented** - 35,000+ words of comprehensive guides
- ✅ **Tested** - 29 validation tests passing (100%)
- ✅ **Flexible** - Works standalone or alongside other applications
- ✅ **Optimal for infrequent use** - Lightweight and efficient

## Summary

Complete TypeScript migration of the Xola UI Kit from PropTypes to TypeScript, along with Node 20 upgrade and ESLint configuration updates. Implemented using Claude Code.

## Migration Statistics

- **JSX/JS Files Migrated**: ~370 files → 0 remaining
- **TypeScript Errors**: 1 (pre-existing in Breakdown.tsx)
- **Lint Status**: ✅ All checks pass
- **Build Status**: ✅ Successful

## Key Changes

### 1. Node 20 Upgrade

**Package & Dependencies:**
- Updated `package.json` engines from Node >=16 to >=20
- Regenerated `package-lock.json` with Node 20 dependencies
- Updated all GitHub Actions workflows to use Node 20

> [!NOTE]
> **Compatibility Note:** The compiled package remains compatible with Node 16+ consuming applications since the output targets ES2020.

### 2. TypeScript Configuration

**`tsconfig.json` Updates:**
- Updated `lib` from ES2020 to ES2022
- Now supports modern features like `.at()` and `replaceAll()`
- Added explicit `types` array to avoid stub package errors

All components have been migrated from PropTypes to TypeScript with proper type definitions:

**Components Migrated:**
- All form components (Input, Textarea, Select, ComboBox, etc.)
- All button components (Button, SubmitButton, ToggleButton, ButtonGroup)
- All DatePicker components (DatePicker, RangeDatePicker, UpcomingDatePicker, etc.)
- All utility components (Phone, Currency, Number)
- All animation components (FadeIn, SlideDown)
- Complex compound components (Modal, Tabs, Sidebar, Popover)
- All other components (Avatar, Badge, Alert, Drawer, Table, etc.)

**Type Patterns Implemented:**
- Interface definitions for all component props
- Enum-like types using `as const` and `keyof typeof`
- ForwardRef components with proper ref typing
- Generic components (e.g., `Search<T>`)
- Proper HTML element prop extensions with `Omit<>` for conflicts

### 4. Code Quality Fixes

- Fixed CSS imports to come after code imports (DatePicker.tsx, ComboBox.tsx)
- Removed unused `ReactElement` import from PopoverList.tsx

**Type Safety:**
- Added explicit type annotations to arrow function parameters in DatePicker components
- Fixed implicit any type errors (TS7006) in RangeDatePicker and UpcomingDatePicker
- Changed logical OR to nullish coalescing in Sidebar.tsx (`leftDrawer ?? rightDrawer`)

## Breaking Changes

None. This is a non-breaking change that maintains backward compatibility.

## Next Steps

After merge:
1. Consumer applications can benefit from full TypeScript types
2. Consider removing PropTypes dependency in a future release
3. Consider migrating Storybook stories to TypeScript
4. Consider enabling stricter TypeScript settings

author: leighmcculloch
body:
### What
Move the broken symlink removal from the "Prepare Test Logs" CI step to the dependencies script that runs during container build. Remove the `docker exec` command that was failing on stopped containers.

### Why
The `docker exec` command requires a running container, so log collection fails when the container exits early due to errors. This prevents debugging intermittent test failures when logs are needed most. Moving the symlink fix to build time ensures `docker cp` always works regardless of container state.

Close #847

author: copilot
body:
The bias detective app required manual session ID entry via input boxes. Updated to match the judge app's automatic authentication pattern using Gradio request query parameters.

## Changes

**Authentication Flow**
- Added `_try_session_based_auth()` to extract session ID from `request.query_params` on page load
- Removed manual login UI (session input, team dropdown, start button)
- Module 0 now visible immediately; authentication happens transparently via `demo.load()`

**State & Function Signatures**
- Changed from `session_state` → `username_state` + `token_state`
- Updated signatures: `ensure_table_and_get_data(username, token, team_name)` instead of `(session_id, team_name)`
- Same pattern for `trigger_api_update()`, `submit_quiz_0()`

**Team Assignment**
- Added `get_or_assign_team()` to fetch from leaderboard before defaulting
- Removes hardcoded team assignment

**Security**
- Generic error logging in auth to avoid exposing exception details

## Example

```python
# Before: manual auth with session_id passed through
def on_start(sess, team):
    token, username = validate_auth(sess)
    data, username = ensure_table_and_get_data(sess, team)
    
# After: automatic auth with username/token from state
def handle_initial_load(request: gr.Request):
    success, username, token = _try_session_based_auth(request)
    team_name = get_or_assign_team(client, username)
    data, username = ensure_table_and_get_data(username, token, team_name)
```

Users access app with `?sessionid=XXX` parameter; authentication handled automatically.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements the SwiftPay theme rebranding and bulk delete functionality for the Task Manager application.

### User Stories Implemented

1. ✅ **As a** user, **I want** the application to display SwiftPay green branding, **so that** the UI reflects corporate identity.
2. ✅ **As a** user, **I want** to see the SwiftPay logo in the header, **so that** brand recognition is consistent.
3. ✅ **As a** user, **I want** to delete all tasks at once with confirmation, **so that** I can quickly clear my task list without deleting individually.

---

## Changes Made

### Backend Changes

#### Three-Layer Architecture Implementation

1. **Repository Layer** (`backend/app/repositories/task_repository.py`)
   - Added `delete_all()` method with SQL `DELETE FROM tasks` operation
   - Proper connection management and error handling

2. **Service Layer** (`backend/app/services/task_service.py`)
   - Added `delete_all_tasks()` method to orchestrate deletion

3. **Routes Layer** (`backend/app/routes/tasks.py`)
   - Added `DELETE /api/tasks` endpoint returning 204 No Content
   - Route placed before `/tasks/{task_id}` for proper matching

4. **Tests** (`backend/tests/test_main.py`)
   - Comprehensive unit tests for the new endpoint
   - Property-based testing using Hypothesis

### Frontend Changes

#### Theme Rebranding
- **Primary Color**: `#667eea` → `#10b981` (emerald green)
- **Secondary Color**: `#764ba2` → `#059669` (darker green)
- Updated all interactive elements: buttons, focus states, loading indicators, checkboxes, hover effects

#### Logo Replacement
- Changed import from `logo.png` to `logo-swiftpay.png`
- SwiftPay logo now displays in application header

#### Delete All Tasks Feature
- **API Service** (`frontend/src/services/api.js`): Added `deleteAllTasks()` method
- **Hook** (`frontend/src/hooks/useTasks.js`): Added `deleteAllTasks` function and `deleteAllLoading` state
- **UI** (`frontend/src/App.jsx`):
  - Delete All button (only visible when tasks exist)
  - Confirmation modal with warning message
  - Loading state during deletion
- **Styling** (`frontend/src/App.css`):
  - Red danger button styling
  - Modal overlay and dialog styles
  - Responsive design for mobile

---

## API Specification

### DELETE /api/tasks

Delete all tasks from the database.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Method | DELETE |
| Path | `/api/tasks` |
| Request Body | None |
| Success Response | `204 No Content` |
| Error Response | `500 Internal Server Error` |

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
The Settings Modal in `ChatPanel.tsx` had a fixed width of 18rem (w-72) and was positioned `right-4`. When the chat panel's width was reduced below ~300px (e.g., via the resizable panel handle or on small screens), the left side of the modal would be clipped by the `overflow-hidden` container.

This change updates the modal's styling to use a calculated width `w-[calc(100%-2rem)]` with a maximum width of `18rem`. This ensures that on narrow screens, the modal shrinks to fit the container (with 1rem margin on each side), while maintaining its original size on wider screens. This fixes the reported "misplaced/incorrect position" bug where components were not visible or aligned properly.

author: regisca-bot
body:
## Summary
Fixes #198 and #166

Two issues were causing card stats to not persist correctly:

### Issue 1: SQLAlchemy JSON mutation detection
The `card_stats` JSONB column was being modified but SQLAlchemy wasn't detecting the change because JSON mutations aren't tracked automatically. Added `flag_modified()` call after updating the `card_stats` dict.

### Issue 2: Starting deck reconstruction
Decks were being reconstructed from the game's end state (`hand + in_play + sleep_zone`) which could be inaccurate (e.g., Copy cards change their name to "Copy of X"). Now capture starting decks at game creation time in a new `starting_decks` field.

## Changes
- **game_state.py**: Added `starting_decks: Dict[str, List[str]]` field to GameState dataclass
- **serialization.py**: Updated serialize/deserialize to persist `starting_decks`
- **game_service.py**: Capture starting decks at game creation; use stored decks in stats with fallback for older games
- **stats_service.py**: Added `flag_modified(stats, 'card_stats')` to ensure SQLAlchemy detects JSON changes
- **fix_card_stats.py**: One-off script to recalculate historical card stats from game playback data (already run)

## Testing
- All 123 existing tests pass
- Manual testing confirmed card stats now increment correctly
- Historical data repair script successfully updated 5 players from 168 game playbacks

body:
Adds developer-only UI allowing repository owner to publish background overrides globally via GitHub API. Personal localStorage-based overrides remain unchanged.

## Changes

**New assets manifest** (`assets/skins/skins.json`)
- 17 background entries mapping IDs to file paths and display names
- Single source of truth for available backgrounds

**Background Manager enhancements** (`js/ui/backgroundManager.js`)
- Loads backgrounds from manifest via `refreshAssetsAndPopulateUI()`
- GitHub token input with optional sessionStorage persistence (`bgmgr.gh_token`)
- Commit message editor with auto-generation (`bgmgr: set manualOverrideId -> <id>`)
- Publish button commits `/bg_override.json` to main branch via REST API (GET for sha, PUT to update)
- Status feedback UI with error handling

**Integration** (`js/ui/introhubBackgroundIntegration.js`)
- Auto-loads manifest on startup to populate dropdown

**Documentation** (`docs/BACKGROUND_MANAGER.md`)
- Token creation workflow
- Security notes (no embedded tokens, sessionStorage lifecycle)
- API usage examples

## Implementation

```javascript
async publishOverrideToRepo(backgroundId, message, token) {
  const owner = 'georgi-cole';
  const repo = 'bbmobile';
  const path = 'bg_override.json';
  
  // GET existing file for sha
  const getUrl = `https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/contents/${path}?ref=main`;
  const existing = await fetch(getUrl, { headers: { Authorization: `token ${token}` }});
  
  // PUT updated content
  const content = btoa(JSON.stringify({ manualOverrideId: backgroundId }, null, 2));
  const putUrl = `https://api.github.com/repos/${owner}/${repo}/contents/${path}`;
  await fetch(putUrl, {
    method: 'PUT',
    headers: { Authorization: `token ${token}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({ message, content, sha: existing.sha, branch: 'main' })
  });
}
```

## UI

Panel requires `localStorage.devBackgroundManager = 'true'` or `?bgmgr=1` query param.

**Full panel:**
![Background Manager Panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c7624f7-073b-4a91-9334-0a428728c4be)

**Error handling:**
![Token validation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b84f204-52d9-43be-b642-4f37f82f546f)

## Security

- No tokens in source
- Token cleared on tab close (sessionStorage only)
- Clear warnings about global impact
- Requires `repo` or `repo:contents` scope

author: copilot
body:
Wake word detection reaches threshold but Home Assistant Assist doesn't launch due to rapid-fire intent attempts and incorrect intent actions.

## Changes

**Cooldown mechanism**
- 3-second cooldown after detection prevents Android from throttling rapid launches
- Wake word scores remain elevated across multiple audio frames (80ms each), causing duplicate launch attempts

**Proper intent chain** (based on HA Android source)
```kotlin
// Method 1: Explicit component with ACTION_ASSIST (primary)
Intent(Intent.ACTION_ASSIST).apply {
    setClassName(HOME_ASSISTANT_PACKAGE, "$HOME_ASSISTANT_PACKAGE.assist.AssistActivity")
}

// Method 2: VOICE_COMMAND action (alternative)
Intent("android.intent.action.VOICE_COMMAND").apply {
    setPackage(HOME_ASSISTANT_PACKAGE)
}

// Fallback chain: Generic ASSIST → Deep link → Main app
```

**Logging**
- Debug logs for each launch method attempt
- Helps diagnose launch failures in production

## Implementation
- `onWakeWordDetected()`: Enforces cooldown before launching
- `launchHomeAssistantAssist()`: Tries multiple intent methods in priority order
- Falls through chain until one succeeds or all fail

author: copilot
body:
Implements a Proof-of-Concept V-JEPA backend demonstrating integration of vision-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture while maintaining API compatibility with existing `/simulate` and `/ingest/media` endpoints.

## Implementation

- **PoC Backend** (`src/sophia/jepa/poc_backend.py`)
  - Implements `JEPABackend` protocol with 768-dim visual/physics embeddings via projection head
  - Basic image feature extraction (PIL-based) + deterministic projections for reproducibility
  - Exponential confidence decay modeling uncertainty accumulation over k-step rollouts
  - Physics-aware dynamics with mass-dependent damping and gravity effects

- **Pluggable Architecture** (`src/sophia/jepa/runner.py`)
  - Backend selection via `JEPA_BACKEND` env var (`stub`|`poc`|`real`)
  - Configuration forwarding: `JEPA_WEIGHTS_PATH`, `JEPA_DEVICE`, `JEPA_DTYPE`
  - PoC uses `v-jepa-poc-v1.0` version identifier vs stub's `jepa-stub-v1.0`

- **Testing & Documentation**
  - 18 tests validating interface compliance, confidence patterns, physics dynamics
  - Interactive demo script (`examples/poc_jepa_demo.py`) with media processing + simulation scenarios
  - Implementation guide with migration path to production V-JEPA

## Usage

```python
import os
os.environ["JEPA_BACKEND"] = "poc"

from sophia.jepa import JEPARunner

runner = JEPARunner()
# Automatically selects PoCJEPABackend, produces 768-dim embeddings
# API unchanged: simulate() and process_media_sample() work identically

result = await runner.process_media_sample(
    sample_id="test", 
    file_path="image.jpg",
    media_type="image",
    metadata={}
)
# Returns visual + physics embeddings, both 768-dim normalized vectors
```

## Design Notes

- **768-dim constraint**: All backends must produce this dimension for Milvus compatibility. Real V-JEPA with different native dimensions requires projection head.
- **Stub remains default**: Zero impact on existing deployments. PoC is opt-in via env var.
- **No GPU required**: PoC runs on CPU with NumPy. Device/dtype config validates for future real backend.

## Related

Integration spec: `docs/research/JEPA/real-v-jepa-integration.md`  
Issue: #75

author: copilot
body:
Implements computer vision logic for ArUco marker detection with scale calibration based on a reference marker (ID 42) affixed to an ISO 7810 credit card.

## Implementation

**Core Detection**
- `ArUcoScanner.detect()` processes `HTMLImageElement | HTMLCanvasElement` through OpenCV.js
- Converts to grayscale and runs `cv.detectMarkers` with `DICT_6X6_250` dictionary
- Returns all detected markers with IDs and corner coordinates

**Scale Calibration**
- When marker ID 42 is detected, calculates `pixelsPerMm` from top edge width (85.60mm standard)
- Enables real-world measurements from pixel coordinates

**Quality Control**
- Compares marker aspect ratio against expected 1.58 (credit card dimensions)
- Sets `isTilted` flag when deviation exceeds 20% tolerance
- Indicates poor viewing angle requiring recapture

**Memory Safety**
- All OpenCV WASM objects (`cv.Mat`, dictionaries, parameters) explicitly deleted in `finally` block
- Critical for browser stability as WASM memory is not garbage collected

## Example Usage

```typescript
import { ArUcoScanner } from '@hail-mary/vision-engine';

const scanner = new ArUcoScanner();
const result = scanner.detect(imageElement);

// result.markers: all detected markers with corners
// result.scaleData?.pixelsPerMm: calibration when ID 42 found
// result.isTilted: true if viewing angle too severe
```

## Package Structure

Standard monorepo TypeScript package at `packages/vision-engine/` following existing patterns (surveyor-engine, shared).

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> I need to create the computer vision logic for a new package: `packages/vision-engine`.
> 
> **Task:**
> Create a TypeScript class called `ArUcoScanner` in `packages/vision-engine/src/scanner.ts`.
> 
> **Dependencies:**
> Assume `opencv.js` is loaded globally as `cv` (declare it as `declare const cv: any;` at the top to satisfy TypeScript).
> 
> **Requirements:**
> 
> 1.  **Constants:** Define the reference object dimensions for a standard Credit Card (ISO 7810).
>     * `ID_CARD_WIDTH_MM = 85.60`
>     * `ID_CARD_MARKER_ID = 42` (We will stick this marker on the back of an ID card).
> 
> 2.  **Method `detect(imageSource: HTMLImageElement | HTMLCanvasElement)`:**
>     * Accept an image source.
>     * Read it into a `cv.Mat`.
>     * Convert to grayscale.
>     * Run `cv.detectMarkers` using the standard dictionary (`DICT_6X6_250`).
>     * Return a result object containing:
>         * `markers`: Array of detected markers (ID + corner coordinates).
>         * `scaleData`: If Marker 42 is found, return the calculated `pixelsPerMm`.
> 
> 3.  **Math Logic (The Calibration):**
>     * If Marker 42 is found:
>     * Calculate the Euclidean distance between its top-left (corner 0) and top-right (corner 1).
>     * `pixelsPerMm = distanceInPixels / ID_CARD_WIDTH_MM`.
> 
> 4.  **Tilt Detection (Quality Control):**
>     * Calculate the aspect ratio of the detected marker (width / height).
>     * Compare it to the expected aspect ratio of a credit card (approx 1.58).
>     * If the deviation is > 20%, add a warning flag to the result: `isTilted: true`.
> 
> 5.  **Memory Management (CRITICAL):**
>     * You MUST call `.delete()` on all `cv.Mat` objects (src, gray, ids, corners) created during the process before returning.
>     * OpenCV WASM does not garbage collect automatically; missing this will crash the browser.
> 
> **Constraint:** Pure logic only. No React hooks. No console logs.
> 


</details>

body:
Unit tests lacked consistent cumulative elapsed time reporting. Tests inheriting from `unittest.TestCase` had no metrics, while tests using the custom `UnitTest` class had partial tracking.

## Changes

- **CumulativeTimeTrackingResult**: Custom `unittest.TextTestResult` subclass that tracks cumulative metrics for all tests
  - Suite elapsed time in minutes (0.1min precision)
  - Completed, passed, and failed test counts
  - Per-test execution time
  - Failed test details with error messages
  
- **CumulativeTimeTestRunner**: Custom runner using the new result class, integrated into `run_all_tests()`

- **Thread-safe state management**: Uses `threading.local()` to prevent race conditions when toggling legacy tracker

After each test completion:
```
2025-12-06 09:51:08 CST | Suite: 0.1min | Completed: 9 | Passed: 9 | Failed: 0
Previous test: test_real_file_operations (...) | Time: 0.001s
```

author: abhaydoes
body:
This PR moves two functions, `solar_angular_radius` and `coordinate_is_on_solar_disk`, from `sunpy.map.maputils` into  `sunpy.coordinates.utils`.

### Motivation

These functions operate entirely on Helioprojective coordinate geometry and do not depend on `GenericMap`.   Their location in `maputils` created an unnecessary coupling between the map and coordinate modules, and their semantics belong in the coordinate utilities layer.

### What this PR does

- Moves the real implementations into `sunpy.coordinates.utils`
- Replaces use of the private function `sun._angular_radius` with the public
  `sun.angular_radius`
- Leaves behind deprecated wrappers in `maputils` to preserve backwards
  compatibility
- Moves and updates tests accordingly

#Move coordinate-only functions from map utils to coordinates utils

Fixes #8445

body:
✅ Phase 2 → Task 3: Implement Module Loader (MVP)

This PR introduces the Module Loader subsystem responsible for discovering, loading, and validating GCD module schemas. It completes the MVP requirements defined in the architecture plan.

⭐ Summary

This PR delivers a fully functional loader that:

Discovers module directories under /modules

Reads and parses schema.json for each module

Integrates with the Phase 2 validator via a dedicated bridge

Produces the canonical LoadedModule structure used by Phase 3 backend and Phase 4 UI

Handles all error cases gracefully (missing schemas, invalid JSON, validation failures)

Provides manual test runners for developer inspection

This work completes Phase 2 → Task 3.

📁 Files Added
Module Loader Core
schemas/core/loader/module-loader.ts
schemas/core/loader/fs-utils.ts
schemas/core/loader/validator-bridge.ts
schemas/core/loader/types.ts

Manual Test Runners
schemas/core/loader/tests/runLoadSingleModuleMockMod.ts
schemas/core/loader/tests/runLoadAllModules.ts


No files outside the /schemas/core/loader/ directory were modified.

🧠 Functional Overview
loadSingleModule()

Reads module directory metadata

Detects and parses schema.json

Calls the existing schema validator

Produces a LoadedModule object with raw schema, validated schema, status, warnings, and validation errors

loadAllModules()

Scans /modules

Loads and validates each module

Returns an array of structured LoadedModule objects

validator-bridge

Normalizes validator output

Prevents crashes if validator throws or returns malformed data

fs-utils

Directory scanning

Schema file detection

Safe JSON reading with error wrapping

🔍 Manual Tests

Added simple Node-runner test scripts that:

Load one module (mockmod)

Load all modules in /modules

Print structured results for developer inspection
(No Jest/Vitest is used in MVP.)

📌 Notes / Future Enhancements (non-blocking)

Optional async FS version

Optional logging hooks (planned for Phase 3)

Optional caching layer

Optional CLI formatting utilities

Optional deeper introspection for future UI generation

These are not required for MVP and do not block this PR.

🟢 Ready for Review

This PR completes all objectives of Phase 2 → Task 3 and is ready for Main Brain approval and merge.

## Copilot Summary
This pull request updates the i18n (internationalization) release workflow and documentation to clarify the process for translation completeness checks and translation freeze periods. It also improves the CLI output for translation coverage. The changes aim to make the release process clearer for both major/minor and patch releases, provide more actionable guidance for contributors and translators, and enhance communication around translation status.

**Documentation and Policy Updates:**

* The i18n workflow in `dev/README_RELEASE_AIRFLOW.md` is rewritten for clarity, distinguishing between patch and major/minor releases, and providing detailed instructions and communication templates for each. The process for announcing and managing translation freezes is clarified, including when freezes are required and how to lift them. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f2ad84d719fff97988402b4162de450904e59c30cbbd7d9bc84889560bcefae8L25-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f2ad84d719fff97988402b4162de450904e59c30cbbd7d9bc84889560bcefae8L89-R199) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-f2ad84d719fff97988402b4162de450904e59c30cbbd7d9bc84889560bcefae8R225-R233) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-f2ad84d719fff97988402b4162de450904e59c30cbbd7d9bc84889560bcefae8L143-R247)
* The definition of an "inactive owner" in `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/README.md` is updated to refer to two consecutive major/minor releases instead of just "releases".
* The section on translation freeze in `airflow-core/src/airflow/ui/public/i18n/README.md` is revised to clarify when and how freezes are announced and enforced, and to specify that freezes apply to the default (English) locale files.

**CLI Output Improvements:**

* The `check_translation_completeness` command now displays the median translation coverage across all languages in the summary table, and uses improved color coding (green for ≥95%, yellow for >90%, red otherwise) for easier visual assessment.

These updates together make the i18n process more transparent, actionable, and user-friendly for both release managers and translation contributors.

author: jbloss1517
body:
The previous implementation called py.import("types") on every iteration
when checking if objects were functions or classes. While Python caches
module imports, this still added unnecessary overhead.

This commit caches the type objects once per function and reuses them
for all type checks within that function's scope:

Performance improvements:
- Cache types.FunctionType once per module instead of per iteration
- Cache builtins.type once per module instead of per iteration
- Eliminate repeated module imports and attribute lookups
- Maintain direct C-level isinstance checks (fast)

The optimization now genuinely outperforms the original approach:

Before (original):
  1. Import inspect once
  2. Get isfunction once
  3. Call isfunction N times (Python function call overhead)

After (optimized):
  1. Import types once
  2. Get FunctionType once
  3. Call is_instance N times (C-level check, no Python call overhead)

Changes:
- Updated is_function() and is_class() to accept cached type objects
- Updated inspect_module() to cache and pass type objects
- Updated load_conftest_fixtures() to cache and pass function_type
- Updated load_builtin_fixtures() to cache and pass function_type
- Updated load_pytest_plugins_fixtures() to accept function_type parameter

This achieves the best of both worlds: correct behavior AND improved speed.

body:
This commit introduces the foundational data and domain layers for the task management feature, following a clean architecture pattern. It sets up the necessary models, data sources, repositories, and use cases for handling tasks.

Key changes include:

- **Dependencies:**
  - Added the `dio` package to handle network requests for the task feature.

- **Domain Layer:**
  - **Entity:** Defined a `Task` entity (`task.dart`) with fields for `id`, `title`, `description`, `status`, and `createdAt`.
  - **Repository Interface:** Created the `TaskRepository` abstract class (`task_repository.dart`) to define the contract for task operations.
  - **Use Cases:** Implemented the `AddTaskUseCase` (`add_task_use_case.dart`) to encapsulate the business logic for creating a new task.

- **Data Layer:**
  - **Model:** Introduced `TaskModel` (`task_model.dart`), which extends the `Task` entity and includes a `fromJson` factory for parsing API responses.
  - **Remote Data Source:** Implemented `TaskRemoteDataSource` (`task_remote_data_source.dart`) to interact with the task-related API endpoints (`/createTask`, `/listTaskByStatus`, `/updateTaskStatus`, `/deleteTask`). It uses the `dio` client for making HTTP requests and handles potential `DioException` and `ServerException` errors.
  - **Repository Implementation:** Added `TaskRepositoryImpl` (`task_repository_impl.dart`), which connects the `TaskRemoteDataSource` to the domain layer's `TaskRepository` interface. It includes error handling to convert exceptions into `Failure` objects.

Took 1 hour 12 minutes

author: kgrgpg
body:
# Security: Eliminate Double-Counting Vulnerability Class via Receipt-Based Accounting

Closes: #N/A (Proactive security hardening based on audit findings)

## Description

This PR introduces a fundamental architectural refactoring of the FlowCreditMarket lending protocol to use **receipt-based accounting** instead of mutable ledger-based accounting. This change leverages Cadence's resource-oriented programming model to **prevent double-counting bugs at the type system level**, ensuring this class of vulnerability cannot recur.

## The Problem: Why the Audit Bug Could Happen Again

During the external audit, a critical double-counting bug was identified in the deposit flow. The issue was fixed in commit `3c3272a` ("Math adjustments from external review"), but **the underlying architectural pattern that allowed this bug to exist remains a systemic risk**.

**The Original Bug (commit 3c3272a):**

```cadence
// BEFORE (buggy):
let depositAmount = from.balance           // Capture balance BEFORE potential split
let uintDepositAmount = FlowCreditMarketMath.toUFix128(depositAmount)
...
// Vault may be split here for deposit limiting, reducing from.balance
...
position.balances[type]!.recordDeposit(amount: uintDepositAmount, tokenState: tokenState)
// Records the ORIGINAL amount, not the actual deposited amount
```

```cadence
// AFTER (quick fix):
let depositAmount = from.balance
...
// Vault may be split here
...
position.balances[type]!.recordDeposit(amount: FlowCreditMarketMath.toUFix128(from.balance), tokenState: tokenState)
// Now records from.balance at the time of recording
```

**Why this class of bug can recur with the current architecture:**

The root cause is the architectural pattern of maintaining a **separate mutable ledger** (`InternalBalance` struct with `recordDeposit`/`recordWithdrawal` methods) that must be manually kept in sync with actual token movements. This pattern:

1. Requires developers to remember to update the ledger at the correct point in time
2. Allows the ledger state to diverge from actual token holdings
3. Creates multiple code paths where synchronization can fail
4. **Does not leverage Cadence's resource safety guarantees**

## The Solution: Receipt-Based Accounting

Instead of maintaining a mutable ledger, this PR introduces **receipt resources** as the single source of truth:

```
OLD PATTERN (Ledger-Based):
--------------------------
Tokens arrive --> Update mutable ledger --> Ledger IS the record
                  (manual, error-prone)

NEW PATTERN (Receipt-Based):
----------------------------
Tokens arrive --> Create receipt resource atomically --> Receipt IS the record
                  (enforced by type system)
```

### Core Principle

A `DepositReceipt` or `BorrowReceipt` resource is created **atomically** when tokens are deposited or borrowed. The receipt:

1. **Cannot be copied** (it's a Cadence resource)
2. **Must be destroyed** to withdraw tokens
3. **Is the record itself** - there is no separate ledger to sync

### New Resource Types

```cadence
access(all) resource DepositReceipt {
    access(all) let poolUUID: UInt64
    access(all) let tokenType: Type
    access(all) let scaledShares: UFix128  // Immutable once created
    access(all) let createdAt: UFix64
    
    access(all) view fun trueBalance(creditIndex: UFix128): UFix128 {
        return FlowCreditMarket.scaledBalanceToTrueBalance(self.scaledShares, interestIndex: creditIndex)
    }
}

access(all) resource BorrowReceipt {
    access(all) let poolUUID: UInt64
    access(all) let tokenType: Type
    access(all) let scaledShares: UFix128  // Immutable once created
    access(all) let createdAt: UFix64
    
    access(all) view fun trueDebt(debitIndex: UFix128): UFix128 {
        return FlowCreditMarket.scaledBalanceToTrueBalance(self.scaledShares, interestIndex: debitIndex)
    }
}
```

### Why This Makes Double-Counting Impossible

With receipts, the deposit flow becomes:

```cadence
// Receipt-based deposit (simplified):
fun depositAndPush(..., from: @{FungibleToken.Vault}, ...) {
    // 1. Split vault if needed for deposit limits
    let actualVault <- splitIfNeeded(<-from)
    
    // 2. Calculate shares based on ACTUAL vault balance (cannot be wrong)
    let shares = calculateShares(actualVault.balance)
    
    // 3. Create receipt ATOMICALLY - the receipt IS the record
    let receipt <- create DepositReceipt(shares: shares, ...)
    
    // 4. Store receipt and deposit tokens together
    position.depositReceipts[type] <-! receipt
    reserves.deposit(from: <-actualVault)
}
```

**It is impossible to record the wrong amount** because:
- The receipt is created from the actual vault being deposited
- You cannot create a receipt without having the tokens
- You cannot access the tokens without destroying the receipt

### Position Structure Change

```cadence
// OLD: Mutable ledger that can get out of sync
access(all) resource InternalPosition {
    var balances: {Type: InternalBalance}  // Mutable struct with recordDeposit/recordWithdrawal
    ...
}

// NEW: Receipt resources ARE the record
access(all) resource InternalPosition {
    var depositReceipts: @{Type: DepositReceipt}   // Resources, not mutable structs
    var borrowReceipts: @{Type: BorrowReceipt}     // Cannot be copied or faked
    ...
}
```

## Changes Overview

### Removed (Legacy Patterns)

- `InternalBalance` struct with mutable `direction` and `scaledBalance` fields
- `InternalBalance.recordDeposit()` method
- `InternalBalance.recordWithdrawal()` method
- `InternalPosition.balances` field

### Added (Receipt-Based Patterns)

- `DepositReceipt` resource
- `BorrowReceipt` resource
- `InternalPosition.depositReceipts` resource dictionary
- `InternalPosition.borrowReceipts` resource dictionary
- Helper functions: `getDepositShares()`, `getBorrowShares()`, `getDepositTypes()`, `getBorrowTypes()`

### Updated Functions

| Function | Change |
|----------|--------|
| `depositAndPush` | Creates `DepositReceipt` atomically with token deposit |
| `withdrawAndPull` | Consumes `DepositReceipt` atomically with token withdrawal |
| `liquidate` | Uses receipts for balance adjustments |
| `healthFactor` | Derives from `PositionView.creditBalances`/`debitBalances` |
| `maxWithdraw` | Uses new `PositionView` structure |
| `buildPositionView` | Populates from receipts, not mutable ledger |
| `quoteLiquidation` | Uses new `PositionView` structure |

### View Layer Refactoring

The `PositionView` struct was refactored to align with the receipt model:

```cadence
// OLD:
struct PositionView {
    let balances: {Type: InternalBalance}  // Single dict with direction
    ...
}

// NEW:
struct PositionView {
    let creditBalances: {Type: UFix128}  // Derived from DepositReceipts
    let debitBalances: {Type: UFix128}   // Derived from BorrowReceipts
    ...
}
```

## Testing

All 89 tests pass:
- FlowCreditMarket submodule: 45 tests
- Main tidal-sc repository: 44 tests

## Benefits

1. **Eliminates double-counting bugs by design** - Cannot record deposits without having the tokens
2. **Leverages Cadence's type system** - Resource linearity enforced by compiler
3. **Simpler mental model** - Receipt IS the record, no separate ledger to sync
4. **Auditability** - Receipt creation/destruction provides clear audit trail
5. **Future-proof** - Pattern resistant to future code changes introducing similar bugs

## Backward Compatibility

This is a breaking change to the internal data structures. External APIs (`PositionDetails`, `PositionBalance`) remain unchanged.

## Critical Files to Review

- `cadence/contracts/FlowCreditMarket.cdc` - Core contract changes
- `cadence/tests/phase0_pure_math_test.cdc` - Updated tests for new `PositionView` structure

## References

- Audit fix commit: `3c3272a` ("Math adjustments from external review")
- Cadence resource documentation: https://cadence-lang.org/docs/language/resources

---

*This refactoring ensures that the class of double-counting bugs identified in the audi

author: jeremywurbs
body:
# Local Cache and Hash Verification for the Registry

## Overview

This PR adds hash verification for registry artifacts and local caching support (#277) for remote registry backends (GCP, MinIO). The optimizations from #299 have not been merged in yet.

## Key Features

### 1. Local Cache for Remote Backends

- **Automatic cache creation**: When using a remote backend (GCP or MinIO), the Registry automatically creates a local cache using a Registry backed by a `LocalRegistryBackend`.
- **Transparent caching**: Cache operations are transparent to users - objects are automatically cached on save/load.
- **Cache directory**: Cache is stored in `~/.cache/mindtrace/tmp/registry_cache_<hash>/` where the hash is derived from the backend URI. I.e. reinstantiating a Registry object to a remote backend will reuse the same cache.
- **Cache invalidation / synchronization**: All Registry artifacts are now hashed on save and verified at every load to ensure the cache is in sync with the remote. Cache metadata is also checked and synced with the remote on all artifact loads. 

### 2. Hash-Based Integrity Verification

- **Hash computation**: SHA256 hashes are computed for all artifacts during `save()` operations.
- **Hash storage**: Hashes are stored in object metadata for later verification.
- **Hash verification**: By default, `load()` verifies artifact integrity by comparing computed hash with stored hash.
- **Corruption detection**: Hash mismatches raise `ValueError` to prevent loading corrupted data. If the mismatch is with the cache, the artifact is automatically reloaded from the remote backend.
- **Configurable verification**: To disable hash verification, pass `verify_hash = False` to the `load()` method.

### 3. Performance Optimizations

As the cache still verifies that the object it has is the same on the remote backend, it must download the metadata from the remote backend to get the hash. Unfortunately, for small objects, the result is that there isn't much performance boost at all.

To actually get the expected performance boost, you'll need to pass `verify_cache = False` to your `load()` calls. Doing so will immediately return any objects in the cache without verifying they are up-to-date from the remote. If the object is not found in the cache, the remote will still be used.

## Technical Details

### New Utility Function

**`mindtrace.core.utils.compute_dir_hash()`**
- Computes deterministic SHA256 hash of directory contents.
- Sorts files by path for deterministic hashing.
- Includes both file paths and contents in hash computation.

### Registry API Changes

**New Parameters:**
- `Registry.load(verify_cache: bool = True)`: Skip remote verification when cache exists.
- `Registry.load(verify_hash: bool = True)`: Enable/disable hash verification.

**New Methods:**
- `Registry.clear_cache()`: Clear the local cache.

**Behavior Changes:**
- `Registry.save()`: Now computes and stores hash in metadata.
- `Registry.load()`: Verifies hash by default, uses cache when available.
- `Registry.delete()`: Also removes objects from cache.

## Testing

### Optional: Disable Cache

To disable caching for a registry:

```python
registry = Registry(backend=remote_backend, use_cache=False)
```

### Optional: Disable Hash Verification

To disable hash verification (not recommended):

```python
obj = registry.load("my:object", verify_hash=False)
```

Hash verification itself should be relatively fast. If performance is an issue because pinging the backend is expensive (even just to get the hash from the metadata), it is likely better to turn off cache verification (below), which will still verify the local cache's hash.

### Optional: Use Cache Without Remote Verification

For performance-critical scenarios:

```python
obj = registry.load("my:object", verify_cache=False)
```

## Example Usage

For the examples below, first log into GCP (`gcloud auth login`) and change the `project_id` and `bucket_name` to be one you have access to.

### Basic Usage (Automatic Caching)

```python
from mindtrace.registry import Registry, GCPRegistryBackend

# Create registry with remote backend - cache is automatically created
gcp_backend = GCPRegistryBackend(
    project_id="mindtrace-test", 
    bucket_name="mindtrace-test-bucket"
)
registry = Registry(backend=gcp_backend)

# Save object - automatically cached locally
registry.save("test:int", 42)

# Load object - uses cache if available, verifies hash
model = registry.load("test:int")  # Still relatively slow, but will not have to redownload the artifact itself

# Load with cache-only (no remote verification)
model = registry.load("test:int", verify_cache=False)  # Fast, does not verify that `test:int` has not changed on the remote.
```

### Hash Verification

```python
# Save computes hash automatically
registry.save("my:data", data)

# Load verifies hash by default
data = registry.load("my:data")  # Raises ValueError if hash mismatch

# Disable verification (not recommended)
data = registry.load("my:data", verify_hash=False)
```

### Performance Example

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from mindtrace.core import TimerCollection
from mindtrace.registry import Registry
from mindtrace.registry.backends.gcp_registry_backend import GCPRegistryBackend
from tests.utils.utils import create_large_file_or_directory

gcp_backend = GCPRegistryBackend(
    project_id="mindtrace-test", 
    bucket_name="mindtrace-test-bucket"
)
registry = Registry(backend=gcp_backend, use_cache=True)

tc = TimerCollection()

# Create a 1GB directory for testing in a temporary directory (auto-cleaned)
with TemporaryDirectory() as temp_dir:
    test_dir = create_large_file_or_directory(
        Path(temp_dir) / "test_large_data", size_mb=1024.0, as_directory=True, num_files=10
    )
    # Save to Registry and time it
    with tc.start("Save to Registry"):
        registry.save("test:large-dir", test_dir)

# *** Test different load scenarios ***

# i. No cache (clear cache first)
registry.clear_cache()
with tc.start("Load without cache"):
    loaded = registry.load("test:large-dir")  # Will automatically save to the cache

# ii. Cache with normal verification (default)
with tc.start("Load with cache"):
    loaded = registry.load("test:large-dir")

# iii. Cache with verify_cache=False
with tc.start("Load with cache (verify_cache=False)"):
    loaded = registry.load("test:large-dir", verify_cache=False)

# iv. Cache with verify_cache=False AND verify_hash=False
with tc.start("Load with cache (verify_cache=False, verify_hash=False)"):
    loaded = registry.load("test:large-dir", verify_cache=False, verify_hash=False)

registry.delete("test:large-dir")

print(tc)
# Save to Registry: 10.057987s
# Load without cache: 5.993713s
# Load with cache: 5.999949s
# Load with cache (verify_cache=False): 1.107502s
# Load with cache (verify_cache=False, verify_hash=False): 0.951978s
```

## Future Enhancements

Some enhancements that have been discussed, but are not included in this PR:

- Cache size limits and eviction policies
- Cache warming strategies
- Background cache synchronization
- Cache statistics and monitoring

## Tests

Tests may be run as usual. `ds test: --unit registry` should return 100% coverage and all pass. Additional tests have been provided in the integration suite. All registry tests may be run with `ds test: registry` and should all pass.
